references.text: God is described as a dwelling or refuge for His people through all generations, which aligns with 'the eternal God is a dwelling' in Deuteronomy.
The shelter of the Most High and the shadow of the Almighty as a refuge correspond to God as a dwelling and refuge.
The eternal God, the Lord, creator of the ends of the heavens, does not grow tired or weary. This connects to 'the arms of the eternal God'.
The Lord is an everlasting rock, reflecting the idea of the eternal God as a refuge.
God drove out nations before Israel, which corresponds to 'He drove the enemy before you'.
God promises to send His fear ahead of Israel and drive out the enemies, which aligns with God driving the enemy away.
Nothing can separate us from God's love, neither height nor depth, which connects to the eternal arms that are beneath us.
The Lord's eternity and unchangeability are emphasized, corresponding to 'the eternal God'.
